headline: Canada's federal government is adding $500 million over five years to a program that helps businesses adopt AI and bring Canadian-made AI products to market.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a funding announcement for a national AI program, reported by CTV News and CBC, but modest in size and mainly about helping businesses adopt AI.
importance_line: Canadian businesses and AI start-ups can draw on more government support, which matters to regional development agencies and to Canada's aim of building its own AI industry, but the reports give no application dates and the money is spread over five years.
summary: CTV News reports that Canada's federal government will make an additional $500 million available over five years to help Canadian businesses adopt artificial intelligence and bring Canadian-developed AI products to market, aimed mainly at health and life sciences, energy and natural resources, transportation, agriculture, manufacturing and robotics. CBC News reports that the money expands the Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative to a total of $700 million, and that one recipient is Deep Breathe, a London, Ontario, company that makes AI software to read lung ultrasounds, which is receiving about $1 million.
